nodes.long_description:
Whirligig is the ultimate VR media player for users who want fully immersive media in the best possible way. Watch 2D, 3D, and 360° content on your Quest headset, with a fully customizable viewing experience.

Key Features

Immersive VR Playback
Purpose-built for VR — perfect for 360° immersive and stereoscopic media, with passthrough support for mixed-reality viewing.

Media Server & Network Streaming
Connect to your Plex or Jellyfin server to stream your personal movie library, with smart local, remote, and relay connection handling. Browse network shares (SMB) on your local network.

Comprehensive 3D Support
Side-by-Side and Over/Under 3D support. Adjustable 3D depth and convergence, and 180°/360° 3D video.

Advanced Playback
Multiple projection modes — Cinema, Fisheye, Equirectangular/Barrel, cubemap, and more.

Customization & Control
Two decoding methods (ExoPlayer, libVLC) for maximum compatibility. Save/load presets per media type, full 5.1 surround sound with positional audio, and subtitle support with external and internal tracks.
nodes.short_description: Whirligig is a powerful media player for VR, supporting 2D, 3D, and 360° content. Compatible with OpenXR-based Quest headsets, it offers adjustable 3D depth, multiple projection modes like Cinema and Fisheye, surround sound, and subtitle support. Stream from your Plex or Jellyfin server, browse network shares, or play local files, with decoding via ExoPlayer or libVLC for a flexible, immersive experience.

nodes.long_description:
Whirligig is a VR media player for the playback and viewing of video and images. It support a wide range of projection types, video support and visual options to make watching your media as enjoyable as possible. 

Main Features
A wide range of projection types including fisheye 90 to 360 degrees, equirectangular, cinema, and custom formats for more unusual projection types including  cubemaps, camera specific projection and many more. All viewable in stereo over under and side by side.
3 render paths to choose from to offer the widest possible video support.
A selection of backgrounds to choose.
Give your media an outer glow.
Subtitle support with accompanying srt files or internal using the Video Lan video path.
16 Save/Load slots to save your position in files and bookmark them for later.
Save media settings into presets to easily switch between projection types.
Bookmark your media so you can easily return to them later.

nodes.change_log:
Subtitles, rebuilt
- Subtitles now sit on a single plane that works correctly in 3D on every video player.
- Subtitles built into MKV and MP4 files (SRT, ASS and MP4 text) now work on every player, not only VLC.
- External subtitle files can be .srt, .ass, .ssa or .vtt.
- Picture-based subtitles (PGS/VobSub, common on Blu-ray rips) are listed and play with the VLC player.
- New "VLC VideoLAN" toggle if you prefer VLC's own subtitle rendering.
- Four fonts, including the dyslexia-friendly OpenDyslexic. Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic and Cyrillic subtitles now show properly instead of empty boxes.
- Outline and drop shadow, or a rounded background box, with a transparency slider and a live preview in the menu.
- New subtitle delay setting: up to 10 seconds earlier or later in 100 ms steps, remembered for each video.
- Subtitles no longer stretch when you stretch the video.
- Much faster loading on large files, and subtitles are cached after the first load.
- Clearer track names, such as "Forced" and "SDH".

Sharper menus
- All the menu text has moved to a new text renderer, so it's crisper at any distance.

Quest
- Smoother performance: lighter rendering of each eye and dynamic foveated rendering.
- Refresh rate menu now shows the rates your headset supports, including 96 and 100 Hz, and your choice is applied every time Whirligig starts.
- Whirligig's own keyboard is now used for logins and search.
- The laser now attaches to your controller straight away on first launch.
- Passthrough fix.
- Updates now refresh the menus and language files properly (French and Portuguese were affected).
- A microSD card or USB drive shows up under "Local" when the headset lets apps read it.

Audio
- New audio delay setting to fix lip sync: up to 1 second either way with VLC, and up to 1 second later with the default player.
- New "VLC 5.1 controls": VLC can now play through Whirligig's positional surround speakers.

Network sources
- SMB: add more than one server with "+ Add server", and remove them one at a time.
- SMB: when a connection fails, Whirligig now tells you why (server not found, share not found, guest access blocked and so on) instead of always blaming the password.
- SMB: fixed sign-in for usernames with accented letters.
- SMB: you can include a share in the address, for example nas/Movies.
- SMB: a wrong username on a Windows PC no longer looks like a successful sign-in, and servers saved by name no longer show as offline when they're online.
- Jellyfin and Emby: Quick Connect lets you sign in by approving a code from another Jellyfin app, with no password to type.
- Jellyfin and Emby: paste the server address straight from your web browser, works with https and redirects, and gives clearer messages for a wrong password, a missing server or an expired session.
- Plex: fixed remote playback through Plex's relay, which often failed on the first try. Sign-in problems are now shown on screen.
- A "Save report" button in each login and settings window saves a connection report to your Downloads folder, ready to send me. Names and public IP addresses are masked.
- If a network video won't play, Whirligig tells you why.
- Servers that aren't answering are marked "(offline)".
- Download to device now works with every video player, not just VLC, and is now available for DLNA too. Turn it on in each source's settings.
- Fixed some MP4 files saying "can't play" on their first download.
- If you quit while watching a network video, Whirligig reopens it next time if the server is reachable, and otherwise opens the browser. SMB videos reopen when you use the VLC player.
- Server passwords and tokens are now hidden in Whirligig's log files.

File browser
- Folders refresh by themselves: new or deleted files appear within a couple of seconds, and files that are still copying wait until they've finished.
- Fixed switching between list and thumbnail view at the top level of a network source.
- Files with the same name on network sources no longer hide each other.

Automatic projection detection
- When it's on, Whirligig now reads the 360/180, fisheye and 3D information stored inside the file (Google and Apple spatial metadata, and MKV tags), not just the filename.
- Better filename tag matching, with several fixes (_OverUnder, swapped-eye tags, _180).
- Only applies the first time you open a file, so a format you've picked by hand is kept.
- Apple spatial (MV-HEVC) videos show a message that they play in 2D.
- It's still off by default.

VR menus
- New grab bar under the menus: point at it and hold the trigger to move the menus around you.
- Hold Reset Orientation for a second to put the menus back.
- New "Disable drag bar" toggle and "Reset UI position" button in Interface > Menu Options.
- The alternative slider menu now moves with Glue UI.
- With 6DoF turned off, the controllers now follow your head instead of freezing in place, and recentring no longer turns head movement back on by mistake.

Languages
- All 12 languages updated, including translations for all the new settings.
- Changing language now updates open menus straight away.

Fixes
- Whirligig no longer gets stuck crashing at launch if the last video was on a network server that isn't available.
- Scrubbing a paused video no longer starts it playing.
- Barrel 360 no longer shows a black area behind you after you've changed the bend.
- Clearing a save slot now shows an empty slot instead of the "missing file" picture.
- Playlists remember their scroll position, skip blank and heading lines, and no longer get forgotten.
- Updated to Unity 6000.6.4f1 and AVPro Video 3.4.3.

Whirligig Media Player — What's New

NEW FEATURES
- Network media browsing: Plex (including remote play), Jellyfin, Emby, SMB and DLNA, with automatic detection of local servers and shares.
- 3D environment fades: the environment now dims during playback in 3D environments (previously 2D only) for better comfort.
- Colour gamut options: new controls in the Quality menu for improved colour reproduction across headsets and videos.
- Player settings presets: save and restore your own Player settings presets, plus three ready-made presets — Default, Desktop VR, and Desktop.

BUG FIXES
- Fixed the Subtitles on/off control not toggling subtitles when bound to an input.
- Fixed crashes when browsing DLNA and SMB network shares.
- Fixed the laser pointer being blocked by backdrop colliders.
- Fixed file explorer issues (menu sizing and opening).
- Fixed the video progress bar when using presets.

NOTE
This is a large update. If a new feature doesn't appear after updating, reinstalling will pull everything in — but note that a reinstall resets Player settings to defaults, so save any custom presets first.

What's New

This release focuses on bugs, performance, and building a foundation for future updates.

PERFORMANCE

- Vulkan rendering: Whirligig now runs on Vulkan for improved stability, better performance, and future-proofing on Android.
- VLC overhaul: Reliability and performance improvements across the VLC pipeline.
- Native thumbnail generation: Video thumbnails now use a native process, vastly improving capture speed.
- Script optimization: All scripts have been reworked to remove bottlenecks.
- Updated dependencies: All plugins, APIs, and SDKs are up to date.

BUG FIXES

Numerous fixes throughout the codebase as a result of the script overhaul.

A NOTE FROM THE DEVELOPER

This is a major update with significant changes under the hood. I've done my best to remove bugs without introducing new ones, but if you spot any issues please let me know at phileday@yahoo.co.uk — your reports are the best way for me to catch what I miss.

If you're enjoying Whirligig, a positive review really helps. And as always, suggestions for future releases are welcome.

Thanks for your continued support.

Happy watching,
Phil
